ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the diagram, point \(C\) lies on segment \(AD\), and \(B\) is the midpoint of \(CD\), with \(AD=13 \, \text{cm}\), and \(BC=3 \, \text{cm}\). If point \(E\) is on line \(AD\), and \(EA=4 \, \text{cm}\), what is the length of \(BE\) in cm?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} As shown in Figure 1, when point E is on segment AC, \\
$\because AB=AC+BC=10\text{cm}$, $EA=4\text{cm}$, \\
$\therefore BE=AB-AE=10-4=\boxed{6}\text{cm}$. \\
As shown in Figure 2, when point E is on the extension line of segment CA, \\
$\because AB=10\text{cm}$, $AE=4\text{cm}$, \\
$\therefore BE=AE+AB=14\text{cm}$. \\
In summary, the length of BE is either \boxed{6\text{cm}} or \boxed{14\text{cm}}.
